# Real-time PCR: curves and Cq — math appendix

<!-- GENERATED by video_studio/scripts/docs.mjs (same code as the video: video_studio/src/lib/qpcr.js) -->

**Illustrative curves — not a real assay, instrument, threshold setting or patient result.** Fluorescence in arbitrary units.

## 1. Model

- F(c) = base + top / (1 + e^(−(c − mid)/slope)), base = 0.05; NTC: base + drift·c.
- Threshold T = 0.2 (illustrative). Cq solved exactly: c = mid − slope · ln(top / (T − base) − 1).
- App card wording (SOURCED, NCBI Bookshelf PCR page): "the key readout is the quantification cycle (Cq) at which fluorescence crosses a threshold; a lower Cq means more starting target"; "roughly doubling the target each cycle".

## 2. Samples

| NTC | — | — | — | none (no crossing) | none | — | — |

NTC signal at cycle 40: 0.066 (stays below the threshold — "no amplification"; the video adds that this alone does not prove a negative, as the app card says).

## 3. Doubling bars

cycle 0: 1 · cycle 1: 2 · cycle 2: 4 · cycle 3: 8 · cycle 4: 16 · cycle 5: 32 (Python: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32). Idealised 2^n for "roughly doubles"; real efficiency is assay-specific and **not** stated.

## 4. What the numbers do NOT mean

- No fold-difference between A and B is claimed (it would require an efficiency assumption).
- No threshold-setting rule, no assay cut-off, no clinical interpretation.
